sources.entry: WiFi Lens - Native open-source Wi-Fi analyzer and network diagnostics app with real-time spectrum scanning, channel congestion visualization, and BLE device tracking. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/SHIINASAMA/wifi-lens) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: WiFi Lens is an open-source native macOS Wi-Fi analyzer and network diagnostics app that scans nearby networks, visualizes channel congestion, and tracks BLE devices.
summary.what_it_does: The open-source edition scans nearby Wi-Fi networks across 2.4, 5, and 6 GHz bands and shows spectrum occupancy with Gaussian channel charts, congestion scores, and regional channel recommendations. It inspects network details such as PHY generation, channel width, 802.11k/r/v, and WPA3, and shows connection info including IP, gateway, DNS, MAC, Tx rate, and security. It offers roaming tests with AP handoff monitoring and session save/load, a per-band channel heatmap, and AP Radar that tracks a selected AP by RSSI with optional audio feedback. It also includes a BLE scanner, a one-click Network Self-Check (path, DNS, HTTPS, proxy; marked Preview), an embedded local MCP server, and PNG/CSV export. The README also describes a separate paid Pro edition with continuous monitoring, history, statistics, and insights, which are not in the open-source edition.
use_cases: Diagnose Wi-Fi channel congestion at home or office
Check which nearby networks support WPA3 or 802.11k/r/v
Test roaming handoffs between access points
Locate a weak access point using RSSI guidance
how_to_run: brew tap ShiinaLabs/apps && brew install --cask ShiinaLabs/apps/wifi-lens
git clone https://github.com/SHIINASAMA/wifi-lens (see README for clone URL)
cd wifi-lens && git submodule update --init ChartLens && cd WiFiLens
notable: Native macOS app with live 2.4/5/6 GHz scanning and spectrum charts
Embedded MCP server bound to 127.0.0.1 so AI assistants like Codex Desktop or Claude Desktop can read local Wi-Fi data
AP Radar tracks a selected access point by RSSI with optional audio feedback
Local-first with no telemetry; scan data stays on the Mac
caveats: Requires macOS 14.6 or later; 6 GHz scanning needs Wi-Fi 6E/7 hardware
Location Services must be enabled for SSID names to be read
Continuous monitoring, event history, statistics, insights, spectrum recording and menu bar monitoring are Pro-only (paid Mac App Store edition)
